summary: Verified PostMePlex AI-character 'relationships + inter-character relay' feature end-to-end + regression on the date/time awareness fix. Backend: created 2 new pytest files (test_relationships_rest.py) and reran test_char_relationships.py (direct) and test_datetime_awareness.py (REST). All 6 backend tests pass. Web UI: logged in as founder (semidiepie/7455), opened Messages > add-ai-character-btn dialog — the new 'Family & friends — link to other characters' section renders, aichar-rel-add is clickable, and after one click aichar-rel-char-0 (character <select>) and aichar-rel-type-0 (relation <input>) appear with the expected test ids. Mobile preview boots clean (no red screen); mobile has no AI-character admin UI, so no mobile parity gap — this is a web-only admin surface by design.
action_items: (Optional, non-blocking) In the dev console on /messages after opening CharacterFormDialog, React logs a hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>'. This is caused by a bundler-injected x-excluded wrapper <span style={display:contents}> rendered inside the <option> for the aichar-rel-char-* <select>. In production (minified) build the x-excluded wrapper is dropped so this is dev-only noise, but if you'd like to silence it, wrap option label via a simple string literal (e.g. {`@${oc.username} - ${oc.name}`}) so the dev instrumentation doesn't try to wrap it. No functional impact — the select still renders and selects values correctly.

(Doc) Heads-up for future tests: the explicit relay matcher (_maybe_relay_to_relative) requires EITHER the relative's first-name token OR the exact relation word (e.g. 'mother') to appear verbatim in the user's text. Synonyms like 'mom' alone are NOT enough. The feature behaves correctly; just worth noting for future reviewers.
critical_code_review_comments: ai_characters.py is 1737 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline; consider splitting (routes vs helpers vs background loops).

The relay keyword list `('tell ', 'message ', 'text ', 'ask ', 'let ', 'know', 'remind', 'send ')` would benefit from a few spoken-synonyms (e.g. 'mom'/'mum'/'dad'/'bro'/'sis') or a lemmatised relation match so natural phrasings like 'tell your mom …' also trigger the relay even when the stored relation is 'mother'. Today the test had to use the exact literal 'mother' for the relay to fire.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (web admin dialog renders expected test ids; mobile boots cleanly)

test_credentials: Founder PIN login — identifier=semidiepie, pin=7455 (web /login). All backend tests use this via POST /api/auth/login-pin.
seed_data_creation: test_relationships_rest.py creates two throwaway characters (TEST_Hope_<uuid> + TEST_Juliette_<uuid>) owned by the founder, with mutual relationships. The module-scoped fixture deletes both characters and clears ai_char_convos / ai_char_messages for those ids on teardown. No persistent data remains.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The new REST test lives at /app/backend/tests/test_relationships_rest.py and takes ~10s (one LLM call). The older direct-DB test (test_char_relationships.py) is still useful for a fast sanity check (<10s) and runs via `cd /app/backend && python tests/test_char_relationships.py`. Known behavioral caveat: /send relay only triggers when the user text contains either (a) the relative's first-name token OR (b) the stored relation word verbatim (e.g. 'mother' not 'mom'). Test characters whose name has an underscore (e.g. 'TEST_Juliette') split() into a single token, so prefer the relation-word path.
rca of the issue: N/A — all tested flows pass. The one initial failure of the REST relay test was a TEST construction bug (user text contained 'mom' but the character's stored relation was 'mother' AND the display name was 'TEST_Juliette_<suf>' which split() keeps as one token, so neither keyword matched). Rewriting the user text with the literal 'mother' made the relay fire reliably. No product bug.
